name: Twist'em
description: Twist'em (Double-Hand Dominoes) is a casino banking game played with a double-six domino set. Each player and the banker receive three tiles and arrange them into a top hand and a bottom hand (pip totals mod 10, nine high). Players bet against the banker; both hands must outrank the banker's two hands to win. Based on Pai Gow but with Western dominoes.

history.origins: Casino table game designed and patented by Olympian Gaming; Western domino version of Pai Gow.
timeline: Early 2000s: Casino table game designed and patented by Olympian Gaming; Western domino version of Pai Gow.
history.cultural: Casino banking game; house or player can bank.
history.evolution: Adaptation of Chinese Pai Gow to double-six domino set for Western casinos.

setup.players: 2-9 (one banker or house banks; up to eight others bet).
setup.dealing: Each player places a bet and receives three tiles; banker receives three tiles.

rules.objective: Form two hands (top and bottom) that respectively outrank the banker's two hands; baccarat-style scoring (pip total mod 10, nine high).
rules.gameplay: Players bet; each receives three tiles and arranges them in a line to form top and bottom hand (totals mod 10). Tiles placed face-down. Banker exposes three tiles and arranges similarly. Compare: player top vs banker top, player bottom vs banker bottom. Both player hands win or one wins and one ties = player wins even money; one wins one loses = push; otherwise player loses. Banker wins ties.
keyRules: Three tiles each; arrange into top and bottom hand
Scoring as Baccarat or Pai Gow: total each hand, drop tens digit; nine high, zero low
If top outranks bottom by mistake, dealer may turn tiles 180 degrees
Banker wins when both hands tie

strategy.basic: Choose arrangement so top and bottom hands are each as strong as possible; avoid the worst arrangement that can be beaten by both others.
strategy.intermediate: Eight ways to play each hand (pairs rotated 180 degrees); decide whether to try for win or push based on odds.
strategy.advanced: Doubles limit possibilities; two or three doubles can be played only one way. House Way is teachable in under ten minutes.
tips: Push percentage is under 22%, lower than Pai Gow; more hands won or lost.
Ranking is easier to learn than Pai Gow.

variations.name: House bank

variations.description: Player-banker position rotates; fee collected prior to deal.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Player bank changes banker rotation only; no engine constant overrides.

scoring.winCondition: Both player hands beat banker's two hands = win even money; one win one tie = win; one win one lose = push; otherwise lose. Banker wins ties.
